caveats: Random-init architecture cost only, encoder alone: no U-Net/policy head, no data loader, no EMA update, no loss beyond output.float().mean(); real per-step cost is this plus the rest of the diffusion policy step.

'fp32' rows use TF32 matmuls (torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('medium') + allow_tf32=True) to mirror the project's own training setting (external/UMI_aquatic/diffusion_policy/config/train_diffusion_unet_timm_umi_aquatic_workspace.yaml:164, applied in workspace/train_diffusion_unet_image_workspace.py:55-60); strict fp32 would be slower.

Precision labels: 'bf16_autocast' = fp32 master weights + torch.autocast(bf16) (what AMP training would do); 'bf16_params' = model.to(bf16), no autocast (marked 'extra' for B/L/H+). ALL 7B rows are bf16_params because the fp32 7B (~27 GB) was never instantiated; the 7B train attempt used pure-bf16 params+grads+AdamW states (no fp32 master, i.e. an optimistic lower bound) and still OOMed at 31.523 GB peak with grad-checkpointing at 32 images -> any real 7B fine-tune (even LoRA with fp32 master) is out of reach on one 32 GB card.

peak_mem_gb = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()/1e9 (allocator view; excludes the CUDA context ~0.5 GB and reserved-but-unallocated slack); on OOM rows it is the peak reached before failure; torch reports the card as 31.37 GiB.
